purpose: Terbinafine is used to treat fungal infections of the nails (fingernails or toenails) and certain skin infections like ringworm or athlete's foot. It works from the inside out by killing the fungus causing your infection. Your doctor may prescribe it when creams or other topical treatments have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Terbinafine works by blocking a substance the fungus needs to build its outer protective layer, called the cell membrane. Without this layer, the fungus cannot survive and dies off. Think of it like pulling away the building blocks the fungus needs to stay alive — it simply cannot keep growing.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include upset stomach, nausea, diarrhea, headache, and rash. Some people notice a mild change in their sense of taste or smell, which usually goes away after finishing the medication. If you develop a serious skin rash or your taste does not return, contact your doctor.
warnings: Terbinafine can rarely cause liver problems, so let your doctor know right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness. It should be used with caution or avoided if you have liver or kidney disease. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, as terbinafine can interact with several other drugs including antidepressants and blood thinners.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose for nail infections is one 250 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day. For toenail infections, treatment typically lasts 12 weeks; for fingernail infections, it is usually 6 weeks. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribed, with or without food.
